bylaw_name: City of Summerside Zoning Bylaw CS-40
notes: Summerside sets the heading above the section number rather than beside it, so the number line is not bold. None of those sections opened a clause and one ran to 33,974 characters, swallowing the zone chapters that follow it. The zone questions here are what that clause was hiding.
expect_sections uses the numbers as the bylaw writes them: 15.1 and 15.2 are provisions of the Low Density Residential zone, and definitions sit under 1.8.
The province-wide development standards regulations appended at page 163 restart numbering at 1, which is why the clause pattern accepts a bare number.

questions.question: How many dwelling units can I have on a lot in the R1 zone?
questions.why: A section whose heading sits on the line above its number. Until that was handled it had no clause of its own.

questions.question: What is the low density residential zone for?
questions.why: Pairs with the question above: both were inside the same oversized clause.

questions.question: What is a secondary suite?
questions.why: Definitions are unnumbered and cite the section that introduces them.

questions.question: Can I add a granny flat to my house?
questions.why: The bylaw says 'accessory dwelling unit', never 'granny flat'. Only semantic retrieval bridges this.
